How to say “NO, THANK YOU” in Vietnamese 🇻🇳✨

Not every situation needs a long explanation! Here are a few simple ways to politely say no in Vietnam:

👋 “Không, cảm ơn!” — No, thank you.
🙏 “Thôi, cảm ơn nhé!” — No thanks, I’m good.
😊 “Mình không cần đâu, cảm ơn bạn!” — I don’t need it, thank you.
🚶 “Không sao, mình tự đi được!” — It’s okay, I can manage on my own.

Save this for your next trip to Vietnam — a little Vietnamese goes a long way! 💛

How to cross the road in Hanoi 🛵

Tip 1: go slow. Walk at a steady pace, don't stop and don't dash. Riders read your pace and go around you.

Tip 2: the plate tells you the city. 29 and 30 are Hanoi. 34 is Hải Dương.

Save this for your first day, and send it to the friend who's still scared of the traffic.

October 10th — A special day for Hanoi. 🇻🇳❤️

On this day in 1954, Hanoi was liberated, marking a new chapter in the city’s history.

72 years later, Hanoi continues to grow, but its spirit, traditions, and stories remain alive in every corner.

From historic landmarks to the little streets we walk every day, there’s so much more to Hanoi than meets the eye.

Don’t just visit Hanoi. Discover its story. 🇻🇳

Ordering food in Vietnam doesn’t have to be complicated 🇻🇳

Just remember: “Cho mình…” = “I’d like…”

🍜 “Cho mình một phở.”
☕ “Cho mình một cà phê sữa đá.”
🥖 “Cho mình hai bánh mì.”

And if you’re not sure what to order, just point at the menu:

“Cho mình cái này.” 👀

One simple phrase, and you’re ready to order like a local.

Save this for your next food stop in Vietnam!
